evidence: deepseek uses "parent" traversal over "adj"; gpt-oss uses "parent_edge"; glm builds an adjacency list and handles the tree recursively. All rely on pruning the unique tree paths connecting required sites.
affordance_in_statement: In this campus, the available cabling options connect all sites, there are exactly n − 1 options, and between any two sites there is exactly one possible cabling route.
removal_suggestion: No wording-only removal is possible without changing the task: the connected n-vertex, n−1-edge, unique-route structure is intrinsically a tree. Defeating these solutions would require allowing cycles or otherwise changing the graph model.

common_affordance: The cabling network is a connected tree, so every pair of sites has one fixed path and the required-site solution is the union of those paths.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DSU/Kruskal-style approach treats the instance like a generic minimum-spanning connectivity problem instead of correctly extracting the minimal required-site subtree. It can include irrelevant branches or fail to account for relay-only vertices and shared paths.

recommended_edit: No valid edit exists under the stated immutable constraints. The only effective change would be to allow a general connected graph with cycles, replacing the tree/unique-route premise; that changes the problem rather than merely re-presenting it.
